hypotheses.name: Certified Causal Slice
hypotheses.claim: Partition each operation's dependencies into native consistency domains; use native atomic snapshot handles inside domains and explicit compatibility witnesses only across independently advancing domains.
hypotheses.falsifier: A broader universal lock is repeatedly equally sound at lower total cost, or domain partitioning admits invalid outcomes under complete dependency declarations.

hypotheses.name: Selection as dependency
hypotheses.claim: Selector/query-plan structure is a causal and authority-relevant read dependency exactly when its mutation can reallocate candidate membership or ranking enough to change the operation.
hypotheses.falsifier: Authorized selector mutations that satisfy the proposed reallocatability criterion do not change selected candidates/effects under controlled trials.

hypotheses.name: SelectionReceipt
hypotheses.claim: Binding selector semantics/version, authorized input view, query plan, candidate-set hash, ranking policy and selected anchors can expose effect-bound selection redirection that record provenance misses.
hypotheses.falsifier: A structural redirection attack changes effect-bound selection while all bound receipt elements remain valid and unchanged.

hypotheses.name: Projection proof obligation
hypotheses.claim: Projection identity hashes are necessary but insufficient; trusted projection semantics require reference/differential/mutation validation.
hypotheses.falsifier: Semantic compiler mutations can be proved impossible by the identity mechanism alone or reference validation adds no detectable protection against controlled semantic faults.

hypotheses.name: Deterministic-before-generative reader ABI
hypotheses.claim: ClayCode should resolve deterministic selection/reduction/version semantics outside the model and project only genuinely unresolved semantics plus receipts.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target Qwen3-4B matched tests show no quality/cost benefit or systematic loss of necessary uncertainty versus raw canonical views.

hypotheses.name: GWT intervention DAG
hypotheses.claim: Graph prior, candidate set, workspace selection, projection, uptake and re-entry should be manipulated as separate causal nodes rather than one GWT on/off switch.
hypotheses.falsifier: Stage-orthogonal interventions provide no improved identification and bundled contrasts remain unbiased under intentionally introduced neighboring effects.

hypotheses.name: Candidate-set receipt dual use
hypotheses.claim: A candidate-set/selection receipt can support both effect security and causal GWT attribution without conflating their evidential claims.
hypotheses.falsifier: The receipt fails either selector-tamper detection or causal replay even when its declared dependency scope is complete.

hypotheses.name: Dual memory trust gates
hypotheses.claim: Persistent memory requires separate ingestion/write authority and retrieval/selection authority because clean stored records may still be unsafely selected and safe selectors may retrieve poisoned records.
hypotheses.falsifier: A single gate is shown to dominate the two-gate design across poisoning and structural-redirection attacks with equal utility/cost.

hypotheses.name: Revocation dependency index
hypotheses.claim: Latent activation should maintain reverse semantic dependencies so revocations invalidate only dependent support instead of globally rebasing the field.
hypotheses.falsifier: Complete transitive dependency tracking costs at least as much as full rebasing or still permits stale support under adversarial derivations.

hypotheses.name: Derived-memory GC
hypotheses.claim: Materialized latent state and currently active/salient state need separate budgets and garbage-collection policies to prevent unbounded derived-memory growth without destroying useful activation.
hypotheses.falsifier: Long-run workloads show one shared budget is equal or better in memory, latency and recall with no stale-state accumulation.

hypotheses.name: Read-aware rematerialization
hypotheses.claim: Incremental overlay vs rebuild decisions should use predicted read demand, query tax, memory, cascade tail and recovery risk rather than a fixed changed-fraction threshold.
hypotheses.falsifier: Across nonstationary workloads a fixed threshold matches or beats the adaptive policy without additional risk.

hypotheses.name: Negative/predicate dependencies
hypotheses.claim: A minimal causal slice must include relevant absence, range, uniqueness and top-k margin predicates, not only positively returned records.
hypotheses.falsifier: Adversarial changes to omitted negative/predicate conditions cannot change operation outcomes when positive reads are unchanged.

hypotheses.name: Immutable epoch publication
hypotheses.claim: Reader-visible derived semantic epochs should publish atomically and reclaim prior epochs only after pinned readers release them.
hypotheses.falsifier: In-place mutation with equivalent synchronization proves lower cost and equal old-or-new semantics under concurrent crash/replay stress.

hypotheses.name: Multi-timescale Android governor
hypotheses.claim: Sustained device policy needs hysteresis over thermal/memory/latency state because burst-optimal context, fanout and speculation settings will not remain optimal under heat and memory pressure.
hypotheses.falsifier: 30–60 minute target-device traces show stationary optimum and no benefit from hysteretic multi-timescale control.

hypotheses.name: Reader identity tuple
hypotheses.claim: Reader experiments must identify model, quantization, context/KV configuration, runtime and projection semantics; parameter count alone is insufficient.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched swaps across these dimensions yield invariant behavior/performance within preregistered tolerance.

hypotheses.name: Tripwires before Pareto
hypotheses.claim: Safety/recovery/authority requirements should be hard feasibility constraints before multiobjective optimization, not soft reward terms.
hypotheses.falsifier: Soft scalar optimization never selects a constraint-violating configuration across adversarial and live workload sweeps while preserving superior utility.

hypotheses.name: Receipted self-reference
hypotheses.claim: Clay self-description should resolve internal references to exact state/epoch/receipt identifiers; prose self-report is not sufficient evidence of current state.
hypotheses.falsifier: Corrupted self-report cannot mislead any downstream operation despite the absence of exact receipt-bound references.

hypotheses.name: Emergence basis certificate
hypotheses.claim: Prospective emergence prediction, lesion, rescue and OOD episodes should carry compatible causal-slice receipts so basis drift is not misclassified as emergent function or failure.
hypotheses.falsifier: Emergence classification remains stable and causally identifiable under deliberate uncontrolled basis drift without such receipts.
